comments.text: Your dashboard updates UI from a background queue and uses UIKit timers – that breaks SwiftUI’s main‑thread model. Add proper @MainActor handling and a Combine‑driven timer, and expose accessibility identifiers.

comments.author: Alex
comments.text: The dashboard now respects SwiftUI’s main‑thread model and uses a Combine‑based timer, which resolves the major concerns. Minor style tweaks are fine, but the functionality is solid, so I’m approving this.

payload.description:
## What Changed
Added a new SwiftUI `TelemetryHealthDashboard` view that subscribes to real‑time telemetry via the existing Kafka client and displays latency and packet‑loss graphs. Integrated the view into the iOS app’s navigation and wired it to Firebase analytics events.

## Why
Provides athletes and coaches immediate insight into connection quality, enabling faster troubleshooting of wearable data streams and improving overall performance monitoring.

payload.text:
Happy to help, Miki. I’ve looked at Chloe’s review on PR‑135 and see the gap around the SwiftUI telemetry health dashboard—specifically the real‑time latency and packet‑loss rendering loop.  

**Pairing:** Let’s set up a 60‑minute session this week. I’m free Tuesday 10 am–12 pm PT and Thursday 2–4 pm PT. Pick a slot that works for you, and I’ll share my screen so we can walk through the current implementation, discuss the performance‑monitoring APIs we use, and refactor the view model to better isolate the telemetry stream.

**Reference material:**  
- Internal doc “Apex Telemetry Architecture” (Confluence → Engineering → Telemetry) – sections 2.3 & 4.1 cover the Combine‑based data pipeline we use for real‑time metrics.  
- Apple’s “SwiftUI Performance” guide (developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/performance) – focus on the “Reducing view recomputation” and “Measuring view rendering time” chapters.  
- The open‑source library **SwiftUICharts** (github.com/willdale/SwiftUICharts) – look at its `ChartData` handling for large, streaming datasets; we borrowed that pattern for our latency graph.

**Growth direction:**  
1. **Deepen SwiftUI & iOS architecture** – mastering view‑model separation, efficient state handling with `@StateObject`/`@ObservedObject`, and profiling with Instruments will make you confident in building any in‑app dashboard. This is the foundation for reliable telemetry on iOS.  
2. **Broaden to cross‑platform telemetry** – once you’re comfortable with the iOS side, extending the same data‑model concepts to our Android and web clients will be much easier. You can start by reviewing the “Telemetry Service Layer” spec (Confluence → Telemetry → Service Layer) which is language‑agnostic.

My recommendation is to close the immediate SwiftUI gap first, then allocate a few weeks to explore the cross‑platform patterns. That gives you solid depth and a clear path to breadth. Let me know which pairing slot you prefer, and I’ll send a calendar invite.
